questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

options.B: a reallocation of resources

options.A: the notes are issued in smaller denominations
options.B: the notes become harder to counterfeit
options.C: the notes become more long lasting
options.D: the notes become unlimited in supply

questions.questionText: What does not cause the demand curve for a good to shift its position?

options.A: advertising expenditure
options.B: consumer tastes
options.C: the price of substitute goods
options.D: the price of the good

options.A: the product is an inferior good the product has a close complement
options.B: the product is an inferior good the product has a close substitute
options.C: the product is a normal good the product has a close complement
options.D: the product is a normal good the product has a close substitute

questions.questionText: In which situation will it be necessary to use an alternative to the price mechanism to allocate a good between consumers?

options.A: Producers of the good receive a subsidy.
options.B: The government imposes a specific tax on the good.
options.C: The government sets a maximum price below the equilibrium price.
options.D: The quantity of the good available is fixed.

questions.questionText: Which policy adopted by an airline is the result of an externality?

options.A: price cutting against rival airlines
options.B: the prohibition of smoking on aircraft
options.C: the provision of different classes of seating accommodation
options.D: the use of internet booking facilities

questions.questionText: What will be the result, from society’s view, if the market price for a product does not reflect the negative externalities in its production?

options.A: too little consumption and too little production
options.B: too little consumption and too much production
options.C: too much consumption and too little production
options.D: too much consumption and too much production

questions.questionText: The table shows some of the costs and benefits, in $ millions, associated with a road building project. Both a government department and a profit-maximising private firm are considering building the road. private external external social costs costs benefits benefits 450 75 50 550 Who would be willing to build the road?

options.A: Both would be willing to build it.
options.B: Neither would be willing to build it.
options.C: Only the government department would be willing to build it.
options.D: Only the private firm would be willing to build it.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to raise the incomes of farmers without raising the price of food to consumers. Which policy should it use?

options.A: a maximum price below the market price for food
options.B: a minimum price below the market price for food
options.C: a payment of a subsidy to farmers to produce food
options.D: a release of government food stocks onto the market

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market supply and demand curves for an agricultural product. The government guarantees producers a minimum price of OX for their output, but allows the market price to be freely determined by demand and supply. supply U X Y Z V W price demand O S T quantity Which area in the diagram represents the total subsidy payments made by the government to producers?

options.A: UYTS B UYZW C XUWV D XYZV

questions.questionText: Why might a government decide to reduce tariffs on agricultural imports?

options.A: to develop greater specialisation
options.B: to increase government revenue
options.C: to promote job creation in rural areas
options.D: to protect small businesses

questions.questionText: A government believes that it can reduce its trade deficit by the introduction of a tax on its main export. When is this likely to be most effective?

options.A: when demand for the export is price elastic
options.B: when the exporting country is a member of a customs union
options.C: when the exporting country is the major world supplier of the product
options.D: when the terms of trade of the exporting country are favourable

The table shows in millions of US$ the balance for four items in a country’s current account for two years. goods services income transfers year 1 –72 84 12 –24 year 2 –87 46 –3 –44 What can be concluded about the changes between year 1 and year 2?

options.A: Income has moved from a net inflow to a net outflow.

questions.questionText: The table gives some information on inflation rates, unemployment rates, and changes in wages for a number of countries in 2006. annual inflation rate unemployment change in country % rate % wages % Britain +1.9 +5.0 +3.5 Germany +2.1 +11.3 +0.8 Italy +2.1 +7.5 +2.3 Japan +0.5 +4.5 –0.6 Spain +4.0 +8.4 +2.5 What can be concluded from the table about 2006?

options.A: Britain had an increase in real incomes.
options.B: High wage rises caused high rates of inflation.
options.C: The price of an identical product was the same in Germany and Italy.
options.D: There were more people unemployed in Spain than in Japan.

questions.questionText: What is not one of the criteria used by the International Labour Office to determine whether a person should be classified as being unemployed when a labour force survey is carried out?

options.A: She is actively seeking employment.
options.B: She is available to take up employment.
options.C: She is eligible to claim unemployment benefits.
options.D: She is currently not in paid employment.

questions.questionText: What is most likely to result from a rising deficit in a country’s balance of payments from increased imports of consumer goods?

options.A: a rise in aggregate monetary demand in the country
options.B: a rise in the country’s aggregate supply
options.C: a rise in the country’s unemployment
options.D: a rise in the international value of the country’s currency
